title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Modernising Business Communications) Bill 2022
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Modernising Business Communications) Bill 2022

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would broaden electronic signing and delivery of business documents, change credit communications rules and replace newspaper notice requirements across several Treasury laws.
Companies and other covered entities could send more documents digitally, while credit customers could choose their preferred delivery format and nominate a contact address.
Relief from sending company documents would depend on unsuccessful efforts to locate members, and the corporations delivery rules would exclude documents sent to regulators.
changes: Electronic signatures would be permitted for every document required or allowed to be signed under corporations law.
Takeover bidders would face civil penalties for misusing security holders' contact information supplied by target companies.
Credit licensees could provide electronic documents without first obtaining individual consent, subject to customer choices and notification requirements.
Newspaper publication rules would be replaced with requirements for notices to be publicly accessible and reasonably prominent.
summary.affected: Companies, fund operators, shareholders, takeover bidders, credit providers and their customers would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Michael Sukkar
speeches.brief: The Treasury Laws Amendment (Modernising Business Communications) Bill 2022 was moved for second reading, modernising several Treasury laws to allow technology-neutral business communications, including electronic signing, flexible document delivery, updated credit communication rules, electronic payment options, and replacement of mandatory newspaper notices with modern methods.
